rules: Score by evidence, not by intention. If you cannot show it in two minutes (a document, a register entry, a dated record), it is not a Yes.
Partly means it exists but is incomplete, untested, undated, or not yet used in practice.
Not applicable is for questions that do not fit your practice (for example, you have no cameras and no employees). Leave it out of the total.
A score is not compliance. It shows where the paper and the practice are far apart. Compliance depends on your facts and your national law.
bands: Most of the programme is missing or only an idea
Modules 1, 3, 5 and 6 first: know what you process, answer requests, handle incidents
Documents exist, but much is untested or incomplete
Practise what you have: training (8), drills (6), provider reviews (9), restore tests (7)
Most things exist and have been used
Close the open items, re-score each year, and look at DPIAs (12) and cameras (10)

questions.question: Is there a one-page description of the practice (size, systems, people, roles, providers) that is kept up to date?
questions.evidence: The description, with a date or version

questions.question: Does it say who the controller is, who the privacy contact is, and who covers when the contact is away?
Are fixed numbers (deadlines, retention periods, owners) set in one place, so that documents do not contradict each other?
questions.evidence: A single source, and a rule for changing it

questions.question: Do patients receive a privacy notice at or before first contact (at the desk and on the website)?
questions.evidence: The notice; where it is shown

questions.question: Does it state the real purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention criteria and rights, matching your record of processing?
questions.evidence: A line-by-line match with the record

questions.question: Does it have a version history and a person who updates it?
Is there a written record of every processing activity, including those with health data (Art. 30)?
For each activity: purpose, legal basis, Art. 9 condition, recipients, retention and security are filled in?
Is the record reviewed at least yearly and whenever a tool or provider changes?
questions.evidence: Review dates in the version history

questions.question: Does every kind of record have a stated retention period and a start date?
Where no law sets a period, is the criterion written down and the period marked as your own choice?
Is deletion carried out and recorded (a destruction register, spot checks)?
Does reception know what to do when someone asks to see, correct or delete data, and pass it on within a day?
Is there a request register with dates and a check of the one-month deadline?
Are there reply templates, including identity checks and reasons for refusing?
Can staff say whom to tell about a mistake or a loss, and how fast?
questions.evidence: A staff rule with a time limit; ask someone

questions.question: Is there a breach register that records every incident, including those not notified, with the reasoning?
Has the procedure been practised in a drill, and reviewed after a real incident?
Are there written rules (accounts, passwords, updates, backups, devices, paper) that fit the practice?
questions.evidence: The policy and the staff pack

questions.question: Is there a list of controls, scored honestly, with an owner and a date for each gap?
Has a restore from backup been tested, and have access rights been reviewed?
Is everyone with access trained before they get it, with a signed record?
Do staff and collaborators sign a confidentiality undertaking?
Is there a yearly refresher, and a short one after each incident?
Is there a list of providers, with each one's role (processor or controller) and the data it reaches?
Is there an Art. 28 agreement with each processor, checked against the Art. 28(3) list?
Has each provider been reviewed (security, location, sub-processors, deletion), with dates?
If you have cameras: is there a written assessment, a camera plan, a short retention period and no cameras where care is given?
questions.evidence: The assessment and the camera plan

questions.question: Are there signs and a notice, a procedure for requests for footage, and an access log?
If you have employees: were they informed and consulted as national law requires, and is it recorded?
Do employees and collaborators receive a notice about their own data, and is receipt acknowledged in writing?
Does it give the basis for each purpose without relying on consent, and the retention?
Is there a joiner and leaver checklist that links accounts, training and retention?
Is there a screening step before any new tool, provider or recording of people?
Are screenings recorded, including the ones that end in "not required", with reasons?
When a DPIA is required: are risks to people scored, conditions given owners and dates, and other documents updated?
